title: Intelligence from Learnable Novelty
author: Yanbo Zhang; Michael Levin
summary: The authors propose that intelligence comes from maximizing "learnable novelty," which means focusing on information a system can actually learn. They show this idea helps systems develop complex, adaptive behaviors like universal computation and image recognition without supervision. Their experiments with neural cellular automata and other models support that maximizing learnable novelty drives intelligent, organized patterns between order and chaos.
